notes: DermRays energy and pulse-power values are calculated from FDA K231910 fluence, working area, and pulse width.
NIRA Model 2 energy values are calculated from FDA K222685 fluence and spot size; FDA lists 2 W max laser power, so pulse-train averaging should be read as an approximation.
Fractional devices are not directly comparable by whole-spot fluence because their relevant variable is microbeam energy and MTZ density.

devices.name: DermRays Revive
devices.evidence_ceiling: FDA substantial equivalence plus marketing study claims; no public controlled Revive wrinkle or pigment trial in K231910

devices.name: NIRA Model 2 / Pro-class
devices.evidence_ceiling: Original NIRA file includes a 76-subject periorbital wrinkle endpoint; Model 2 uses substantial-equivalence bench/usability testing

devices.name: NIRA Beauty Skin Laser / Precision-class
devices.evidence_ceiling: 76-subject periorbital wrinkle clinical endpoint in FDA K163137

devices.name: Tria SmoothBeauty / FRX
devices.source: FDA K130459 and local Tria IFU
devices.evidence_ceiling: Fractional 1450nm periorbital wrinkle device; compare by microbeam energy and coverage density, not whole-spot fluence

devices.name: Cynosure Elite+ 1064nm predicate context
devices.source: FDA K141425 and K231910 predicate table
devices.fluence_j_cm2_context: K231910 lists 12 J/cm2 under a 15mm handpiece spot and 4.7 J/cm2 under a 24mm handpiece spot for the predicate comparison; professional platform has broader clinical flexibility than this table captures.
